quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When visibility is reduced, what should you do first?

options.text: Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.explanation: Slowing down is the first thing you should do when you cannot see well. This keeps you safe on dangerous roads.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is ahead.

questions.question: Two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time. Who goes first?

options.text: The car on the left must let the car on the right go first.
The car on the right must let the car on the left go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left must let the car on the right go first.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time to an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The left driver can go when it is safe.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ colored and show direction and distance information.
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background. They show you directions and distances to places you want to go. They are helpful when driving in new areas.

questions.question: When you pass a large vehicle in a small car, what should you prepare for?

options.text: Strong wind from the large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller cars off course. Be ready to steer correctly when passing or going near large vehicles.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow line to pass another car?

options.text: Only if no cars are coming toward you.
Only if the car ahead is going slower than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: You cannot pass over a double solid yellow line. You can only cross these lines when turning into a driveway or business entrance. No passing is allowed over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: What does a stop sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop if cars are coming.
Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Go through carefully without always stopping.
Stop only if traffic is on the cross road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must stop completely. Let vehicles and pedestrians pass. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow in a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is not used in traffic signals.
It means the same thing as a red traffic light.
Drivers can turn in the direction the arrow points.
Traffic must stop and stay stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a red traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a circular red light. You must stop and cannot turn in that direction.

questions.question: You want to turn left at a green light but traffic is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Wait at the edge of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Wait in the middle of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Go because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the middle of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When turning left with oncoming traffic, you can enter the intersection on a green light to get ready. Wait in the middle until traffic clears, then turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A steep downhill slope is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep downhill slope is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep downhill grade is coming.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes use arrows to control turns from specific lanes. What does a solid yellow arrow mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
Drivers may turn in the direction shown by the arrow.
A green arrow will appear next.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the same thing as a yellow traffic light. Slow down and be ready to stop when you see it.

questions.question: Before turning left, what is most important?

options.text: Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic gets a red light.

questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic light, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass before you turn.

questions.question: What shape and color is a slow-moving vehicle emblem?
questions.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is an orange triangle. These vehicles are traveling at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed from the side with the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the side with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the side with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass only from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: When driving on snow-covered roads, what is the minimum following distance?
questions.explanation: On snow-covered roads, keep at least six seconds of distance between your vehicle and the car ahead. Always increase your following distance on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow. They tell drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign warns you that a steep hill is ahead. Slow down and be ready to adjust your speed.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Places where you must always stop.

questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and instructions from flaggers. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads, which must yield?
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on the right. This applies at all intersections.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you always do?

options.text: Start signaling as you move into the next lane.
Signal at least 500 feet ahead on residential streets.

questions.explanation: Cars and motorcycles can hide in your blind spot. Glance over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet before changing lanes in residential areas, or five seconds before on freeways.

questions.question: What do round signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Round signs warn drivers of railroad crossings ahead. Use extra caution when you see these signs.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you to do?

options.text: You can pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
You can pass if you know what is ahead.
You can pass, but only at night.

questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It is white and rectangular with black text. You must follow all instructions on regulatory signs. This sign means passing is not allowed.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, what should you do?

options.text: Return to your lane when you have enough space between you and the car you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to your lane when you have enough space between you and the car you passed.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, move back to the right side when there is enough space between you and the car you passed.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer going 55 mph needs up to ____ feet to stop completely.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take much longer to stop than cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer needs about 400 feet to come to a complete stop at 55 mph.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while driving, what should you do first?

options.text: Shift to a higher gear and press the gas pedal.
Shift to a lower gear and pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a lower gear and pump your brakes.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail, shift to a lower gear and pump the brake pedal to build up pressure and stop. Then find a safe place to pull over and do not drive the car again until the brakes are fixed.

questions.question: What does this sign above your lane mean?

options.text: You can either continue on the freeway or exit from your current lane.
You can stay in your lane and continue on the freeway.
You must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means that lane will leave the freeway. You cannot continue straight. You can either change lanes to go through the interchange or you must exit.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up beside the front car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up beside the front car.
questions.explanation: First, check traffic and signal. Stop alongside the car in front of the empty space. Then turn your wheels and park.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway or to make a U-turn where allowed.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe when backing your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn before shifting into reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you sit down in the driver's seat.
Turn up the radio to alert people around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you sit down in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Walk to the back of the car before getting in to check for children and objects.

questions.question: When should you slow down when exiting a highway?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
When you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane early. Do not slow down until after you enter the exit lane.

questions.question: To prevent crashes, a driver should be alert, be prepared, and:
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, use this formula: be alert, be prepared, and act in time.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: A speed that is faster than reasonable and safe.
A speed that is safe for current conditions.

questions.explanation: You must not drive faster than is reasonable and safe. Adjust your speed based on traffic, weather, pedestrians, road condition, and lighting. You must also obey all posted speed limits.

questions.question: What is the safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down when entering, speed up when exiting.
Keep the same speed throughout the curve.
Speed up when entering, slow down when exiting.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when entering, speed up when exiting.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you enter a curve and gradually increase speed as you exit. Speeding up as you enter makes it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: The Child Passenger Safety Law requires children under age 4 and weighing less than ____ pounds to use an approved safety seat.
questions.explanation: Children under age 4 and weighing less than 40 pounds must be in an approved safety seat. The seat can be rear-facing or forward-facing with a five-point harness and must be in the rear seat.

questions.question: On unmarked rural roads, the speed limit is:
questions.explanation: The speed limit on unmarked rural roads is 50 mph. Follow posted speed limits if they differ from this.

questions.question: Signs for public recreation areas are:
questions.explanation: Brown signs show areas for cultural, historical, or public recreation purposes. They help you find places when traveling in unfamiliar areas.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, you should:

options.text: Wait until another driver waves you on.

questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. However, you must first let any pedestrians or traffic still in the intersection pass safely.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is okay to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with a single rider.
When passing a motorcycle, you must move completely into the left lane.
A motorcycle's brake lights always turn on when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: When passing a motorcycle, you must move completely into the left lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need a full lane of space. Your vehicle must be fully in the left lane before you pass a motorcycle.

questions.question: On a multilane highway, slower traffic should drive in:

options.text: The lane with the least traffic

questions.explanation: Use the right lane if you are driving slower than other traffic. The left lane is for faster traffic that is passing slower vehicles.

questions.question: This sign shows:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that an intersection with a crossing road is ahead.

questions.question: Another driver is trying to pass your car. What should you do?

options.text: Signal to the other driver when it is safe for them to pass.
Look for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane when another driver passes you on the left. Look for oncoming traffic and slow down so the passing vehicle can move back into the right lane easily.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
Motorcycle drivers are less skilled than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see than cars. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away they are or how fast they are going. Always watch for motorcycles and be extra careful around them.

questions.question: When making a left turn, what should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: Before turning left, signal and slow down. Do not cut the corner short. This can hit other vehicles.

questions.question: You come to an intersection with a flashing red light. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left since the road is blocked ahead.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop. Then you can go when the way is clear.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection but see no stop line or crosswalk. Where should you stop?

options.text: You are not required to stop.
Slow down to check if crossing traffic is clear.
Stop where you can see 200 feet on each side, even if you enter the roadway.
Stop where you can see approaching traffic before entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you can see approaching traffic before entering the roadway.
questions.explanation: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop at the closest point where you can see traffic coming. Do not enter the roadway to get a better view.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something unexpected. Talk to other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians. Use your signals when slowing down, stopping, or turning. Use your horn when needed.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, what should you do?

options.text: Always have the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are near.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are near.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a vehicle that is close may not have time to stop.

questions.question: What color are highway signs that show the distance to the next exit?
questions.explanation: Signs that tell you where to go are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the harder your vehicle will hit if there is a crash.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.
Drivers may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. A dashed white line means you can cross it to pass or change lanes if it is safe.
